<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><a name="Parti_170147"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">PART&nbsp;I</font></b></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><a name="Item1_Business_170149"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 1.&#160;
Business</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h5 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-decoration:underline;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">General</font></u></h5>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cascade Natural Gas
Corporation (Cascade or the Company) was incorporated under the laws of the
state of Washington on January&nbsp;2, 1953.&#160;
Its principal business is the distribution of natural gas to customers
in the states of Washington and Oregon.&#160;
Approximately 72% of its residential and commercial gas distribution
margins are from customers in the state of Washington.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of September&nbsp;30,
2005, the Company had approximately 196,000 residential customers, 30,000
commercial customers, and 719 industrial and other larger customers.&#160; Residential, commercial, and most small
industrial customers are generally core customers who take traditional &#147;bundled&#148;
natural gas service, which includes supply, peaking service, and upstream
interstate pipeline transportation.&#160;
Sales to core customers in fiscal 2005 accounted for approximately 24%
of gas deliveries and 71% of operating margin.&#160;
The Company&#146;s sales to its core residential and commercial customers are
influenced by fluctuations in temperature, particularly during the winter
season.&#160; A warm winter season will tend
to reduce gas consumption.&#160; Also
affecting sales to core customers is the addition of more energy-efficient
homes and facilities, consumer behavior driven by cost increases and a desire
to conserve, and a recent trend to warmer winters in the Company&#146;s service
areas.&#160; Together, these forces have
resulted in reductions in average gas usage per customer.&#160; The company is actively working with
regulators within both states served to develop restructured rates to offset
this trend.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Non-core customers are
generally large industrial and institutional customers who have chosen &#147;unbundled&#148;
service, meaning that they select from among several upstream supply, pipeline
transportation, and gas management service options independent of the Company&#146;s
distribution service.&#160; The Company&#146;s
margin from non-core customers is derived primarily from distribution service
and to a lesser extent from gas management service revenue.&#160; Gas management service revenue primarily
includes operating margin from delivery of gas supplies and fees charged to
non-core customers in consideration of securing gas supplies and pipeline
capacity for the customers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Natural Gas Supply</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The majority of Cascade&#146;s
supply of natural gas is transported via Williams Gas Pipelines - West
(Williams).&#160; Williams owns and operates a
transmission system extending from points of interconnection with El Paso
Natural Gas Company and Transwestern Pipeline Company near Blanco, New Mexico
through the states of New Mexico, Colorado, Utah, Wyoming, Idaho, Oregon and
Washington to the Canadian border near Sumas, Washington.&#160; Natural gas is transported north from the
Colorado and New Mexico area, and south from British Columbia, Canada.&#160; The Company is also a shipper on the
transmission system of Gas Transmission Northwest Corporation (GTN), owned by
TransCanada Pipeline (TCPL). GTN connects with the facilities of the TCPL at
the international border near Kingsgate, British Columbia and extends through
Washington and central Oregon into California. In addition, Cascade receives
natural gas directly from Duke Energy Gas Transmission (DEGT) at the Canadian
border near Sumas, Washington and also intra British Columbia at a receipt
point known as Station 2 on DEGT.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Presently, baseload
requirements for Cascade&#146;s core market are provided by eight major gas supply
contracts with various expiration dates ranging from 2006 through 2009 and
averaging 460,000 therms per day of Canadian supply and 106,500 therms per day
of domestic supply.&#160; These contracts are
supplemented by various service agreements to cover periods of peak demand
including three storage agreements.&#160; One
such agreement, with Williams, extends to October&nbsp;31, 2014 and provides
for 167,890 therms per day and a maximum, renewable inventory of 6,043,510
therms.&#160; The second storage agreement is
with Avista Energy, and has a primary term ending April&nbsp;30, 2006 and
entitles Cascade to receive up to 150,000 therms per day and a maximum,
renewable inventory of 4,800,000 therms.&#160;
A third contract, also with Williams for liquefied natural gas (LNG)
storage, is effective through October&nbsp;31, 2014.&#160; Under this LNG agreement, Cascade is entitled
to receive up to 600,000 therms per day to a maximum inventory of 5,622,000
therms.&#160; In addition to withdrawal and
inventory capacity, Cascade maintains a corresponding amount of firm
transportation from the storage facility to the city gate for each of these
agreements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company enters into various seasonal and annual gas supply contracts
designed to match the load requirements of its customers.&#160; Interstate pipelines provide natural gas to
the Company from production areas in the Rocky Mountain states and from western
Canada. Management believes gas supply resources in those areas are adequate to
serve the Company&#146;s current needs and to support future growth.&#160; The</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">3</font></p>

<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">wholesale price of gas in the region has increased in recent years,
paralleling national trends.&#160;
Additionally, a favorable differential that has historically existed
between Pacific Northwest gas prices and national prices has narrowed as new
pipelines have increased access to Rocky Mountain and Canadian supplies by
California and mid-west markets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">To mitigate price volatility,
the Company employs a gas procurement strategy for supplies for sale to core
customers that involves entering into physical gas supply contracts with
suppliers at published first-of-the-month index prices for up to five-year
terms.&#160; To mitigate the price volatility,
these index related supplies are hedged through the use of derivatives,
primarily swaps, with financial institutions.&#160;
Approximately 90% of the core market&#146;s requirement for fiscal 2006, 60%
of fiscal 2007, and 30% of fiscal 2008 are secured with fixed prices as of the
end of fiscal 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h5 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-decoration:underline;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">State Regulation</font></u></h5>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s rates and
practices are regulated by the Washington Utilities and Transportation
Commission (WUTC) and the Oregon Public Utility Commission (OPUC).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cascade&#146;s gas supply contracts
contain pricing provisions based on market prices, and as a matter of practice,
the Company generally enters into derivatives, generally swaps, to fix the
price of future supplies.&#160; To the extent
that overall demand is different from the amount of gas supply under contract
and hedged, the net effective price paid by Cascade may change with respect to
supplies purchased for core customers.&#160;
The Company is able to pass the effect of such changes, subject to regulatory
review, to its customers by means of a periodic purchased gas cost adjustment
(PGA) in each state.&#160; Gas price changes
occurring between times when PGA rate changes become effective are deferred for
pass through in the next PGA.&#160; These PGA&#146;s
include interest compensation on any deferred collections financed by Cascade.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">With respect to such gas
supplies delivered to Oregon customers, 67% of the incremental change in the
actual cost of gas supplies, as compared to the forecasted cost reflected in
the PGA, is deferred.&#160; The remaining 33%
(increase or decrease) is absorbed by the Company. This mechanism is intended
to encourage the Company to seek opportunities to lower its cost of supplies
and to be innovative in its management of the supply portfolio to avoid price
spikes.&#160; Cascade&#146;s gas supply portfolio
for Oregon core customers is comprised mostly of gas supplies with commodity
prices that have been fixed through derivative arrangements; therefore,
management believes the risk or opportunity for the Company is not significant
under the 67% / 33% sharing arrangement.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cascade has an earnings
sharing mechanism with respect to its Oregon jurisdictional operations as
required by the Oregon Public Utilities Commission.&#160; The mechanism was designed as an incentive to
pursue operational efficiencies and new revenue opportunities, and to share the
success of such pursuits with ratepayers if the Company&#146;s earnings exceed a
calculated ceiling.&#160; Under that
arrangement, the Company is authorized to retain all of its earnings
attributable to its Oregon operations up to a threshold level equal to 300
basis points above a 10.25% return on equity (ROE).&#160; Subsequent years&#146; base ROE is adjusted by 20%
of the movement in the average of the annual yields, reported monthly, for
five-, seven-, and ten-year US&nbsp;Treasury debt securities for the test
period.&#160; If the adjusted Oregon earnings
are below the threshold, there is no rate adjustment.&#160; If the adjusted earnings are above the
threshold, one-third of the earnings exceeding the threshold will be refunded
to customers through future rate reductions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is also
subject to state regulation with respect to integrated resource planning, and
its most recent update of its Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) was filed in 2004
with both the WUTC and the OPUC.&#160; The IRP
shows the Company&#146;s optimum set of supply and demand side resources that
minimizes costs and risk over the 20-year planning horizon.&#160; The IRP also sets forth possible core
customer growth scenarios for a 20-year period.&#160;
In addition, the IRP sets forth the Company&#146;s demand side management
goals of achieving certain conservation levels in customer usage.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The IRP also includes the
Company&#146;s supply side management plans regarding transportation capacity and
gas supply acquisition over a 20-year period.&#160;
The Company develops updates of the IRP every two years.&#160; These updated documents take into account
input solicited from the public and the WUTC and OPUC staffs.&#160; While the filing of the IRP with both
commissions gives the Company no advance assurance that its acquisitions of
pipeline transportation capacity and gas supplies will be recognized in rates,
management believes that the integrated resource planning process benefits the
Company by giving it the opportunity to obtain input from regulators and the
public concurrently with making these important strategic decisions.&#160; Until the Company receives final regulatory
approval of these decisions in the context of the ratemaking process, the
Company cannot predict with certainty the extent to which the integrated resource
planning process will affect its rates.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Like virtually all U.S.
gas utilities, Cascade has experienced a declining trend in per-customer
consumption over the last several years.&#160;
Given the drivers, this trend is unlikely to reverse itself.&#160; To date, growth in the number of residential
and commercial customers and earnings from other services contributed to
offsetting this reduction.&#160; The company
is working with regulators in each state served to develop decoupling
approaches which enable gas utilities to promote conservation while still
earning an adequate return on its invested capital and operating costs.&#160;&#160; Similar approaches have been implemented in
Oregon and many other states.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h1 align="left" style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:left;"><b><u><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">Pipeline Safety</font></u></b></h1>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cascade
is subject to both state and federal pipeline safety rules.&#160; In both Washington and Oregon, the federal rules&nbsp;are
enforced by the state commissions.&#160; Both
the federal and state rules&nbsp;are updated and amended periodically.&#160; The Pipeline Safety Act of 2002 requires
operators of gas transmission pipelines to identify lines located in High
Consequence Areas (HCA&#146;s) and develop Integrity Management Programs (IMP&#146;s) to
periodically inspect the integrity of the pipelines and make repairs or
replacements as necessary to ensure the ongoing safety of the pipelines.&#160; The legislation requires Cascade to complete
inspection of 50% of the highest risk pipelines located in its HCA&#146;s within the
first five years, and the remaining covered pipelines within 10 years of the
date of enactment.&#160; The Pipeline Safety
Act also requires re-inspections of the covered pipelines every seven years
from the date of the previous inspection for the life of the pipelines.&#160; Cascade has met all interim deadlines in The
Act and is on schedule&nbsp;to meet remaining deadlines.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Federal Energy
Regulatory Commission (FERC) Matters </font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Cascade is not subject to regulation by the FERC; however,
FERC actions can affect the amounts Cascade pays to interstate pipeline
companies for interstate deliveries of natural gas supplies.&#160; Several issues are pending before FERC, or
are on appeal before the U.S. Court of Appeals.&#160;
The final outcome may affect prices Cascade pays; however, none would
have a significant impact.&#160; Since the
Company&#146;s current tariffs with the WUTC and OPUC provide for 100% pass through
of costs subject to FERC regulation, the Company expects that the final
resolution of pending issues will not significantly affect net income.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Curtailment
Procedures</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In some previous heating
seasons, cold weather has required Cascade to curtail deliveries to its
interruptible customers. Cascade has not curtailed any supply to firm
customers, except under rarely occurring force majeure conditions. Cascade&#146;s
tariffs effective in Washington and Oregon allow for curtailment of
interruptible services, which are provided at rates lower than for firm
services.&#160; In the event of curtailment by
Cascade of firm service due to force majeure, Cascade&#146;s tariffs provide that it
will not be liable for damages to any customer for failure to deliver gas
curtailed in accordance with the provisions of the tariffs.&#160; The tariffs provide for appropriate
adjustment of the monthly charges to firm customers curtailed by reason of an
insufficient supply of gas.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h5 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-decoration:underline;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Territory Served
and Franchises</font></u></h5>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
population of communities served by Cascade totals approximately 1,045,000. At
the end of September&nbsp;2005, Cascade held the franchises necessary for the
distribution of natural gas in all of the communities it serves in Washington
and Oregon. Under the laws of those states, incorporated municipalities and
counties may grant non-exclusive franchises for a fixed term of years
conferring upon the grantee certain rights with respect to public streets and
highways in the location, construction, operation, maintenance and removal of
gas distribution facilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
the opinion of Cascade&#146;s management, none of its franchises contain any
restrictions or requirements that are of a materially burdensome nature, and
such franchises are adequate for the conduct of Cascade&#146;s present business.
Franchises expire on various dates from fiscal 2006 to 2065. Management has not
incurred significant difficulties in renewing franchises when they expire and
does not expect any significant problems in the future.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h5 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-decoration:underline;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Customers</font></u></h5>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Residential
and commercial customers principally use natural gas for space heating and
water heating.&#160; Once connected, these
customers rarely change from gas service.&#160;
This category is our fastest growing with customer count increases of 3-5%
during each of the last several years.&#160;
The residential and commercial</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">5</font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">market
is very weather-sensitive.&#160; See &#147;Seasonality&#148;
below.&#160; In addition to the seasonal
nature of usage, average consumption per customer has declined since the
beginning of this decade.&#160; As mentioned
earlier, the addition of more efficient homes and other buildings, replacing
old appliances with more efficient units, and consumer behaviors drive this trend.&#160; Reductions are most pronounced following
significant gas cost increases.&#160; Cascade&#146;s
growth has contributed to offsetting these declines.&#160; As discussed under State Regulation, the
Company is working with regulators in both states served to restructure rates
to recognize this trend.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Agreements
with Cascade&#146;s principal industrial customers are for fixed terms of not less
than one year and provide for automatic extension from year to year unless
terminated by either party on at least 120-days&#146; notice.&#160; The principal industrial activities in Cascade&#146;s
service area include the production of pulp, paper and converted paper
products, plywood, industrial chemicals; refining of crude oil; the processing,
flash freezing and canning of many types of vegetable, fruit and fish products;
processing of milk products; meat processing; drying and curing of wood and
agricultural products; and electric power generation.&#160; Electric generation customers represent a
significant portion of industrial revenues.&#160;
The demand for gas-fired generation tends to vary with the availability
of hydroelectric power and the relative price of gas.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Seasonality</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Weather is an important
factor affecting gas revenues because of the large number of customers using
gas for space heating.&#160; For the fiscal
year ended September&nbsp;30, 2005, 68% of operating revenues and 106% of
income from operations were derived from the first two quarters (October&nbsp;2004
through March&nbsp;2005). Because of the seasonality of space heating revenues,
financial results for interim periods are not indicative of results to be
expected for an entire year. To mitigate the seasonality of space heating
revenues, the Company pursues a marketing strategy of encouraging the
installation of appliances that utilize natural gas more consistently
year-round since they are not as influenced by weather conditions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Competitive
Conditions</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cascade
operates in a competitive market for natural gas service.&#160; Cascade competes with residual fuel oil and
other alternative energy sources for industrial boiler uses, and oil, propane,
and electricity for residential and commercial space heating, and electricity
for water heating.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Competition
is primarily based on price.&#160; Though
wholesale natural gas prices have increased significantly during 2005, Cascade&#146;s
residential and commercial rate schedules continue to maintain a price
advantage over oil in its entire service territory and have an advantage over
electricity in much of its territory.&#160; In
addition, natural gas enjoys the advantage of being the preferred energy choice
by builders for new home construction.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
large volume industrial market has always been very sensitive to price
fluctuations between the comparable cost of natural gas and alternate fuels,
principally residual fuel oil used in boiler applications.&#160; However, the advent of open access
transportation in the late 1980&#146;s and early 1990&#146;s and the subsequent
restructuring of gas supply and contractual provisions with these customers
have improved the Company&#146;s competitive position. With the escalation of
wholesale natural gas prices that began in the 2000 - 2001 heating season, and
again in 2005, the Company has experienced some movement of its gas load to
alternative fuels and some plant curtailments by industrial customers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
addition to multiple alternative fuels, the Company is subject to bypass.&#160; Bypass refers to actual or prospective
customers who install their own facilities and connect directly to an upstream
pipeline and thereby &#147;bypass&#148; the Company&#146;s distribution service.&#160; The Company has in the past experienced
bypass, but has also experienced success in offering competitive rates to
reduce economic incentives to bypass.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company competes with others in acquiring gas supplies for resale to
governmental and industrial customers.&#160;
Further </font>opportunities in this area will be dependent upon market
conditions that can change over time, credit worthiness of customers and the
increase or decrease in the number of competing providers that are available.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) is a major supplier of hydroelectric
power in the Pacific Northwest including Cascade&#146;s service area.&#160; BPA significantly influences the electric
rates of all classes of customers including those applications in direct
competition with natural gas marketed by Cascade.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">6</font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">

<hr size="2" width="100%" noshade color="gray" align="left">

</font></div>

<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Environmental</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is subject to
federal and state environmental regulation of its operations and properties
through the United States Environmental Protection Agency, the Washington
Department of Ecology and the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality.&#160; Such regulation may, at times, result in the
imposition of liability or responsibility for the clean up or treatment of
existing environmental problems or for the prevention of future environmental
problems.&#160; For detailed descriptions of
specific environmental issues, see &#147;Environmental Matters&#148; under Item 7.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Capital
Expenditures</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Driven by Cascade&#146;s high
growth rate, capital expenditures are primarily used to expand the Company&#146;s
distribution system to serve new customers. Investments to expand capacity and
to assure a safe and reliable system require a relatively smaller portion of
our overall capital spending.&#160; A one-time
project, the installation of automated meter-reading capabilities system-wide,
represented $16 million of our capital spending during fiscal years 2003 and
2004.&#160; Total capital expenditures for the
three fiscal years ended September&nbsp;30, 2005 averaged approximately $31.5
million.&#160; Capital spending for fiscal
2006 is expected to be significantly lower, likely within or slightly higher
than the range Cascade spent during fiscal years 1999 to 2002.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cascade has no current
plans for major one-time capital projects.&#160;
Also supporting the reduced need to invest capital is the Company&#146;s
practice of assuring that its spending generates the highest possible returns
within the shortest possible time, while assuming prudent risk, and complying
with the requirements of regulators.&#160; An
example is our practice of working with developers and new customers to share
the cost of marginal expansions and service connections when projected returns
are insufficient for the Company to fund the entire investment.&#160;&#160; Other practices include considering
innovative solutions to specific needs, such as utilizing temporary supplemental
capacity rather than investing in expensive pipe expansions to cover peak
requirements.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Non-Utility
Subsidiaries</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cascade has four
non-utility subsidiaries, only two of which are actively engaged in business at
present. The first active subsidiary, Cascade Land Leasing, is engaged in the
servicing of loans that were made to Cascade&#146;s gas customers to finance their
purchases of energy-efficient appliances.&#160;
The subsidiary ceased making new loans in September&nbsp;1997.&#160; In addition, Cascade Land Leasing receives a
small amount of annual royalty on gas production in Colorado. These mineral
rights were a result of historical operations the Company had in Colorado until
the mid-1970&#146;s. The second active subsidiary, CGC Resources, is engaged in
pipeline capacity management, with the objective of mitigating gas costs for
Cascade.&#160; The subsidiaries, which in the
aggregate account for less than 1% of the consolidated assets of the Company,
do not currently have a significant impact on Cascade&#146;s financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Personnel</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At September&nbsp;30,
2005, Cascade had 375 employees.&#160; Of the
total employees, 177 are represented by the International Chemical Workers&#146;
Union.&#160; The present contract with the
union extends to April&nbsp;1, 2006 and remains in force thereafter from year
to year unless terminated by either party by written notice sixty days prior to
the expiration date.&#160; Historically, the
Company and the union have negotiated a new agreement to become effective as of
the earliest expiration date rather than allowing the existing agreement to
remain in force.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;23,
2005, 29 customer service representatives in the Company&#146;s Bellingham and
Sunnyside call centers elected to be represented by the International Chemical
Workers&#146; Union.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h5 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-decoration:underline;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Available
Information</font></u></h5>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company makes
available free of charge, on or through its website, http://www.cngc.com, its
annual, quarterly and current reports, and any amendments to those reports, as
soon as reasonably practicable after electronically filing such reports with
the Securities and Exchange Commission. In addition, copies of these documents
may be requested, at no cost, from the Company&#146;s corporate headquarters.
Requests should be directed to Shareholder Relations, Cascade Natural Gas
Corporation, 222 Fairview Avenue North, Seattle, WA 98109, or by phone at 206-624-3900.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><a name="Item2_Properties_170154"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 2.&#160; Properties</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At
September&nbsp;30, 2005, Cascade&#146;s utility plant investments included
approximately 5,244 miles of distribution mains ranging in diameter from two
inches to sixteen inches, 215 miles of transmission mains ranging in diameter
from two inches to twenty inches, and 3,593 miles of service lines.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
distribution and transmission mains are located under public property such as
streets and highways or on private property with the permission or consent of
the individual owner.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cascade
owns 21 buildings used for operations, office space and warehousing in
Washington and six such buildings in Oregon. It leases two commercial offices
and warehouse buildings.&#160; Cascade
considers its properties well maintained and in good operating condition, and
adequate for Cascade&#146;s present and anticipated needs. All facilities are
substantially utilized.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><a name="Item3_LegalProceedings_170156"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 3.&#160; Legal Proceedings</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Incorporated herein by
reference is the information under &#147;Environmental Matters&#148; in Item 7.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><a name="Item4_SubmissionOfMattersToAVoteO_170158"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">No matters were submitted
during the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:left;text-decoration:underline;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">Executive Officers of the Registrant</font></u></b></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><a name="Item7_ManagementsDiscussionAndAna_170210"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item
7.&#160; Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis
of Financial Condition and Results of Operations</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Restatement of Financial Statements</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Subsequent to the
issuance of the financial statements for the year ended September&nbsp;30,
2004, management determined that the Company&#146;s deferred income tax liabilities
were not correctly stated as of September&nbsp;30, 2004, 2003, 2002, and
2001.&#160; Further, the Company&#146;s provision
for deferred income taxes was not correctly stated for the years ended September&nbsp;30,
2003, 2002, and 2001 under accounting principles generally accepted in the
United States of America (&#147;GAAP&#148;).&#160; As a
result, beginning retained earnings, financial position, results of operations,
and cash flows have been restated.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">See Note&nbsp;3 to the consolidated financial
statements of this Report for a summary of the effects of these changes on the
Company&#146;s consolidated balance sheet as of September&nbsp;30, 2004, as well as
on the Company&#146;s consolidated statements of income and comprehensive income, shareholders&#146;
equity and cash flows for fiscal year 2003.&#160;
The accompanying Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis gives effect to
these corrections.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following is management&#146;s assessment of the
Company&#146;s financial condition and a discussion of the principal factors that
affect consolidated results of operations and cash flows for the fiscal years
ended September&nbsp;30, 2005, 2004, and 2003.&#160;
References herein to 2005, 2004, and 2003 refer to these fiscal years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h6 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">Overview</font></u></b></h6>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is a local
distribution company (LDC) serving approximately 227,000 customers in the
States of Washington and Oregon.&#160; Its
service area consists primarily of relatively small cities and rural
communities rather than larger urban areas.&#160;
The Company&#146;s primary source of revenue and operating margin is the
distribution of natural gas to end-use residential, commercial, industrial, and
institutional customers.&#160; Revenues are
also derived from providing gas management and other services to some of its
large industrial and commercial customers.&#160;
The Company&#146;s rates and practices are regulated by the Washington
Utilities and Transportation Commission (WUTC) and the Oregon Public Utility
Commission (OPUC).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Key
elements of the Company&#146;s strategy:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Remain focused on the natural gas
distribution business.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Pursue appropriate regulatory
treatment, including initiatives to decouple the Company&#146;s earnings from
changing customer consumption patterns, and remove other regulatory impediments
to effective management of the business.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Economic expansion of its customer
base by prudently managing capital expenditures and ensuring new customers
provide sufficient margins for an appropriate return on the new investment
required to acquire the customers.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Continue to focus on operational
efficiencies.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Manage cash flow to avoid the
requirement of additional debt financing.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Opportunities and
Challenges</font></b></h2>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company operates in a
diverse service territory over a wide geographic area relative to the Company&#146;s
overall size and number of customers.&#160;
The economies of various parts of the service area are supported by a
variety of industries and are affected by the conditions that impact those
industries.&#160; Management believes there
are growth opportunities in the Company&#146;s service area, especially in the residential
and commercial segments.&#160; Factors
contributing to these opportunities include low market penetration in many of
the towns served, and general population growth in the service area, including
some areas of rapid growth.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Overall
revenues and margins are also negatively impacted by higher efficiency in new
home and commercial building construction, higher efficiency in gas-burning
equipment, and customers taking additional measures to reduce energy
usage.&#160; The increasing cost of energy in
recent years, including the wholesale cost of natural gas, continues to
encourage such measures.&#160; The Company
continues to believe that energy efficiency and conservation are the most
viable near-term tactics for influencing the wholesale natural gas prices.&#160; It&#146;s also a vital strategy for stabilizing
the cost of gas over the long term.&#160; The
traditional</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">13</font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">

<hr size="2" width="100%" noshade color="gray" align="left">

</font></div>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">regulatory
establishment of rates ties the recovery of cost to volumetric sales.&#160; This traditional rate design creates a
financial disincentive for utilities to promote conservation.&#160; The Company is working with regulators and
other stakeholders in each state to develop an acceptable decoupling mechanism
that will enable the Company to promote conservation while still earning an
adequate return on its invested capital and operating costs.&#160; Similar approaches have been implemented in
many states and are endorsed by a variety of organizations, including the
recent endorsement by the National Association of Regulated Utility
Commissions.&#160; The results of such rate
requests and other initiatives for regulatory relief are subject to significant
uncertainties.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company earns
approximately one third of its operating margin from industrial and electric
generation customers.&#160; Loss of major
industrial customers, or unfavorable conditions affecting an industry segment,
could have a detrimental impact on the Company&#146;s earnings.&#160; Many external factors over which the Company
has no control can significantly impact the amount of gas consumed by
industrial and electric generation customers and, consequently, the margins
earned by the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenues and margins from
the Company&#146;s residential and small commercial customers are highly
weather-sensitive.&#160; In a cold year, the
Company&#146;s earnings are boosted by the effects of the weather, and conversely in
a warm year, the Company&#146;s earnings suffer. &#160;Peak requirements also drive the need to
reinforce our systems (i.e., increase capacity).&#160; Our operations group considers innovative
approaches such as temporarily utilizing mobile gas supply rather than making
large investments in long-term capacity increases, which may not be fully
utilized.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Prospects for continuing
strong residential and commercial customer growth are excellent.&#160; The pace of new home and commercial
construction remains steady in communities served by the Company.&#160; Good potential also exists for converting
homes and businesses located on or near the Company&#146;s current lines to gas from
other fuels, as well as for expanding the system into adjacent areas.&#160; Customer count growth in this sector has been
about double the average of U.S. gas utilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our customer service call
center organization recently voted to accept union representation.&#160; The company plans to negotiate an agreement
that will support our effort to cost-effectively provide superior customer
service.&#160; The timing and results of
negotiations are uncertain.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The contract with the
union representing our service mechanics and construction staff expires on April&nbsp;1,
2006.&#160; Again, we plan to negotiate an
agreement that supports superior and cost-effective customer service.&#160; The results and timing of negotiations are
uncertain.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We continue to pursue
operating efficiencies and cost reductions.&#160;
During fiscal 2004, we completed the implementation of automated meter
reading capability covering our entire service area.&#160; This reduced our staffing needs by 27
full-time equivalent positions.&#160; During
fiscal 2005, the centralization of our customer service activities and
organization reductions, enabled by a variety of other improvements, reduced
our staffing by over 9%.&#160; Our current
organization is able to service more customers at a lower cost than in prior
years.&#160; Changes completed during fiscal
2005 alone resulted in improving our customer-per-employee ratio from 500 to
600.&#160; We continue to look for additional
operating improvements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As discussed in Item 1
(our description of the business), we carefully analyze the economics of our
spending to support growth.&#160; When
justified under our tariffs, we work with developers, business owners and
residents to share certain construction costs to assure a fair return to
Cascade.&#160; Non-revenue-generating spending
is also managed to assure that we use the most economically attractive
solutions while providing for a safe and reliable system.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management
continuously seeks improvement opportunities in all areas.&#160; Our discussion above covering regulatory
change, labor relations, operating practices, our organization and our
investment to maintain and expand our gas delivery system are examples.&#160; We will continue to evaluate these and other
aspects of our business to improve our customer service and the returns to our
shareholders.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">OPERATING MARGIN</font></u></b></h2>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><u><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">2005 Versus
2004</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Residential and Commercial</font></u> &#150; Operating margin<b><font style="font-weight:bold;"> </font></b>(revenue
minus gas costs and revenue taxes) is primarily a function of customer growth
and gas usage per customer.&#160; The net
addition of approximately 10,500 billed residential and commercial customers in
2005 contributed approximately $3,160,000 of additional margin compared to fiscal
2004.&#160; This was mostly offset by
reductions in gas usage per residential and commercial customer of 3.8% and
4.4%, respectively, which reduced margins by $2,550,000.&#160; The addition of more efficient homes and
businesses, reduced consumption per consumer, and slightly warmer weather
compared to last year drove the lower consumption rates.&#160; Weather statistics indicate that fiscal 2005
was 1% warmer than fiscal 2004 and 4% warmer than the average of the past five
years.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Industrial</font></u>
&#150; Margin from natural gas deliveries to industrial customers decreased by
$717,000 year to year.&#160; This reduction is
due to a variety of reasons including contract changes reducing minimum
requirements, a decline in the number of customers and reduced usage by several
sectors including chemical and paper manufacturing.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Electric Generation</font></u>
&#150; Margin from natural gas deliveries to electric generation customers
decreased $350,000 for the year with the decline attributable to lower-cost
hydroelectric supplies and the increased wholesale price of natural gas.&#160; Looking ahead, gas usage by generation
customers will continue to depend on the variables of regional demand for
power, availability of hydro resources, and the relationship between the market
price of electricity and the cost of gas.</p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">16</font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">

<hr size="2" width="100%" noshade color="gray" align="left">

</font></div>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Gas Management</font></u> &#150;
Gas management services margin was down $1,877,000 from last year.&#160; The Company has lost sales and margin as a
result of increased competition for the sale of gas supplies to large-volume
customers.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Oregon Earnings
Sharing</font></u> &#150; The change in Oregon Earnings Sharing amounts are
the result of revised estimates of liability for refunds to Oregon customers
related to OPUC requirements.&#160; As of the
end of 2004, the Company estimated its liability to be $525,000.&#160; Based on a final analysis approved by the
OPUC, 2004 earnings were not sufficient to trigger a sharing with customers,
and in 2005 this $525,000 was reversed.&#160;
Management also estimates that there will be no liability for 2005.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><u><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">2004 Versus
2003</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><u><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Residential and
Commercial</font></u><font size="2" color="black" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;"> &#150; Margins from residential and
commercial customers increased $3,208,000.&#160;
Of this increase, approximately $2,200,000 resulted from the increase of
8,013 in the average number of customers billed.&#160; The remaining increase stemmed primarily from
increased gas usage per customer, related to somewhat cooler weather.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Industrial</font></u>
&#150; For the year, gas distribution margins from industrial customers were
essentially the same as 2003.&#160; In the
first half of the year, industrial distribution margin showed signs of recovery
from the stagnation that followed the 2000 energy crisis and a prolonged
recession.&#160; However, the upward trend
stalled in the third quarter, and in the fourth quarter, margins declined
compared to 2003. The primary reason for the reversal of the positive trend is
believed to be the higher wholesale prices of natural gas.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Electric Generation</font></u>
&#150; Margins from electric generation customers were down $1,019,000 in
2004 compared to 2003.&#160; Much of the
decline was due to an abundance of cheap hydroelectricity and moderate regional
demands for power during the first part of the year.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><u><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Gas Management</font></u><font size="2" color="black" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;"> &#150; Margins from providing gas management services decreased $515,000 in
2004 from 2003.&#160; Margins in 2003 were negatively
impacted by an $865,000 contract termination charge.&#160; Absent this factor, gas management margin
would have decreased by $1,380,000 in 2004.&#160;
</font><font size="2" color="black" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The re-emergence of energy marketers, an industry segment
that all but disappeared in the wake of the Enron failure, resulted in stiff
competition for gas supply sales to larger gas customers.&#160; Cascade has lost customers to such marketers,
and margins that are available for any sales are smaller than in the past.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h4 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-decoration:underline;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">COST OF OPERATIONS</font></u></b></h4>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><u><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">2005 versus 2004</font></u></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The primary drivers of the $3,683,000
(9.1%) increase in operating expenses are organizational changes in 2005.&#160; Costs of $1,234,000 were recognized related
to the replacements of the Company&#146;s Chief Executive and Chief Financial
Officers.&#160; The expenses were primarily
made up of severance compensation for the retiring executives, hiring expenses,
and signing bonuses for the new executives.&#160;
In the fourth quarter of 2005, the Company eliminated 22 employee
positions resulting in $1,121,000 in severance expenses.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Operating expenses in 2005 included
the write off of $596,000 in capital projects determined to no longer be
viable. The projects were primarily related to development of computer software
applications.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Purchased services expenses in 2005
were higher by $532,000 compared to 2004. The primary driver of this increase
is the costs related to the Company&#146;s Sarbanes-Oxley compliance work, with
increased costs of $337,000 over 2004.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Bad debts expense increased $325,000
over 2004.&#160; Driving this increase are
higher gas costs resulting in higher customer bills.&#160; Management believes the increase also stems
in part from the transition of customer service and collections activities from
15 offices to a single consolidated customer service call center.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Employee benefits expense decreased
$625,000.&#160; The primary drivers of the
decrease were reductions in medical and dental expenses, for active employees,
and in retiree medical expense.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Depreciation and amortization expense
increased $949,000 reflecting higher depreciable assets resulting from capital
spending.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">17</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><u><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">2004 versus 2003</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Compared to 2003, overall Cost of
Operations was $3,823,000 lower for the year.&#160;
Within Cost of Operations, notable changes in Operating Expenses
included the reduction in employee benefits expenses of $4,448,000.&#160; The comparison is affected by retirement plan
curtailment charges of $1,451,000 in 2003.&#160;
The remaining decrease is primarily attributed to changes in benefit
plans initiated in 2003, designed to reduce costs.&#160; Benefits expense in 2004 was also favorably
impacted by recognition of $315,000 for the Medicare prescription drug subsidy,
reflected as a reduction in retiree medical expense. In addition, 2003 expenses
included a $524,000 severance cost.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The $987,000 increase in depreciation
and amortization is primarily related to increases in depreciable gas
distribution system assets.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">INCOME
TAXES</font></u></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The changes in the
provision for income taxes from 2004 to 2005, and from 2003 to 2004 are
primarily attributable to the changes in pre-tax earnings.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h1 style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">OTHER
COMPREHENSIVE INCOME (LOSS)</font></b></h1>

<h1 style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h1>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
comparisons of Other Comprehensive Income (loss) from 2005 to 2004, and from
2004 to 2003 are related to minimum pension liability adjustments. In 2005 and
2004, the value of pension plan assets continued a modest recovery from the
declines experienced in 2001 and 2002. As a result of this recovery, the
Company has reduced its accrual related to its unfunded accumulated benefit
obligation by $177,000 and $1,270,000 for 2005 and 2004.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h6 align="center" style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">LIQUIDITY AND CAPITAL
RESOURCES</font></b></h6>

<h6 align="center" style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h6>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The seasonal nature of
the company&#146;s business creates short-term cash requirements to finance customer
accounts receivable and construction expenditures.&#160; To provide working capital for these
requirements, the company has a $60,000,000 bank revolving credit
commitment.&#160; This agreement has a
variable commitment fee and a term that expires in October&nbsp;2007.&#160; The company also has a $10,000,000
uncommitted line of credit. As of September&nbsp;30, 2005, there was
$12,500,000 outstanding under these credit lines.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Due to the nature of
Cascade&#146;s business, which is characterized by reliable payments from a stable
customer base and our expectations that capital spending will be reduced from
the last few years, we expect to have limited need to source additional capital
during fiscal year 2006.&#160; For this
reason, combined with the availability of short-term credit and the ability to
issue long-term debt and additional equity, management believes it has adequate
financial flexibility to meet its anticipated cash needs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The table below shows the
Company&#146;s future commitments under contractual obligations as of September&nbsp;30,
2005:</font></p>

<h3 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">OPERATING ACTIVITIES</font></u></b></h3>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The 2005 decline in net income
contributed to lower net cash provided by operating activities.&#160; A significant factor is reflected in
Deferrals of gas cost changes, resulting from higher wholesale gas costs</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
