<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">paid this year relative to the amount
built in to customer rates.&#160; This
outpaced the amount of $5,098,000 from Amortization of gas cost changes.&#160; In October&nbsp;and November&nbsp;2005, the
Company implemented new rates designed to collect from customers the amount of
fiscal 2006 gas costs, plus a temporary component designed to recover
approximately $12 million of previously deferred gas costs.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Significant
factors affecting non-cash components of net income are prepaid income taxes
and deferred income taxes.&#160; In the fourth
quarter of 2004, the Company received Internal Revenue Service approval of an
application to change the method of accounting for deferred gas costs for
purposes of calculating current federal income taxes.&#160; As a result, the Company is able to deduct on
its federal tax returns amounts included in deferred gas cost charges.&#160; This change is effective retroactive to the
tax return for fiscal year 2001, and in 2005, the Company filed amended tax
returns for its fiscal years 2001 and 2002.&#160;
Accordingly, the Company has accrued an estimated refund of federal and
state income taxes for those years of $7.5 million. These refunds represent
temporary differences between book and taxable income, and deferred income
taxes have been accrued so that there is no impact on net income resulting from
this change.&#160; As deferred gas cost
charges are amortized in future years, the Company&#146;s income tax liability and
cash payments for income taxes will increase accordingly.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">INVESTING ACTIVITIES</font></u></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Net
capital expenditures for 2005 were approximately 28% lower than last year.&#160; The decrease is primarily attributable to
$12,515,000 expended in 2004 on a project to install electronic devices on all
the Company&#146;s customer meters to allow for automated meter reading (AMR.).&#160; The AMR project was begun in 2003 and
completed in 2004 with total expenditures on the project of approximately
$16,198,000.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h4 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-decoration:underline;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">FINANCING ACTIVITIES</font></u></b></h4>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company retired $14
million in current maturities of long-term debt during 2005 and $22 million
during 2004.&#160; These retirements were
funded with two debt issues totaling $45 million during 2005.&#160; None of the outstanding long-term debt
matures during fiscal 2006.&#160;
Additionally, during 2005, the Company reduced its short-term debt by
$21 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Proceeds
from issuance of common stock are primarily issuance of new stock through the
dividend reinvestment plan, 401(k) plan, and on exercise of stock options.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h6 align="center" style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS</font></b></h6>

<h6 align="center" style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h6>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There are two claims
against the Company for cleanup of alleged environmental contamination related
to manufactured gas plant sites previously operated by companies that were
subsequently merged into the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The first claim was
received in 1995 and relates to a site in Oregon.&#160; An investigation has shown that soil and
groundwater contamination exists at the site.&#160;
There are parties in addition to the Company that are potentially liable
for cleanup of the contamination.&#160; Some
of these other parties have shared in the costs expended to date to investigate
the site, and it is expected that these and other parties will share in the cleanup
costs.&#160; Several alternatives for
remediation of the site have been identified with preliminary estimates for
cleanup ranging from approximately $500,000 to $11,000,000.&#160; It is not known at this time what share of
the cleanup costs will actually be borne by the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The second claim was
received in 1997 and relates to a site in Washington.&#160; An investigation has determined that there is
evidence of contamination at the site, but there is also evidence that other
property owners may have contributed to the contamination.&#160; There is currently not enough information
available to estimate the potential liability associated with this claim, but
the Company and other parties may become more involved in investigations of the
nature and extent of contamination, and possible remediation of the site, as
increased interest has been expressed concerning its potential for
redevelopment.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management
first intends to pursue reimbursement from its insurance carriers.&#160; In the event the insurance proceeds do not
completely cover the costs, management intends to seek recovery from its
customers through increased rates.&#160; There
is precedent for such recovery through increased rates, as both the WUTC and
the OPUC have previously allowed regulated utilities to increase customer rates
to cover similar costs.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">19</font></p>

<h2 align="center" style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">EFFICIENCY
INITIATIVE &#150; CUSTOMER SERVICE CALL CENTER</font></b></h2>

<h2 align="center" style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In January&nbsp;2005, the
Company began operation of a customer-service call center at its existing
district office in Bellingham, Washington.&#160;
Activation of the call center was phased in, and it became fully
operational in March&nbsp;2005.&#160; This
call center consolidated, in one location, the Company&#146;s customer service
function, which had been spread through 15 offices.&#160; To implement the call center, the Company
incurred $855,000 capital expenditures and $313,000 transitional expenses.&#160; After factoring in the transitional expense,
there was a small net decrease in expense compared to 2004.&#160; Management expects fiscal 2006 to benefit
from a full year of approximately $750,000 in reduced costs, in addition to
improved customer service.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 align="center" style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">CRITICAL
ACCOUNTING POLICIES</font></b></h2>

<h2 align="center" style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company&#146;s financial statements are prepared in accordance with accounting
principles generally accepted in the United States of America (GAAP).&#160; In following GAAP, management exercises
judgment in selection and application of accounting principles.&#160; Management considers Critical Accounting Policies
to be those where different assumptions regarding application could result in
material differences in financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">USE OF ESTIMATES</font></u></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The preparation of financial statements in
conformity with GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that
affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, and disclosure of
contingent assets and liabilities, at the date of the financial statements, and
the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period.&#160; The Company has used estimates in measuring
certain deferred charges and deferred credits related to items subject to
approval of the WUTC and the OPUC.&#160;
Estimates are also used in the development of discount rates and trend
rates related to the measurement of retirement benefit obligations and accrual
amounts, allowances for doubtful accounts, unbilled revenue, valuation of
derivative instruments, and in the determination of depreciable lives of
utility plant.&#160; On an ongoing basis,
management evaluates the estimates used based on historical experience, current
conditions, and on various other assumptions believed to be reasonable under
the circumstances.&#160; Actual results may
differ from these estimates under different assumptions or conditions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">REVENUE RECOGNITION</font></u></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">The Company recognizes operating revenues based on
deliveries of gas and other services to customers.&#160; This includes estimated revenues for gas
delivered but not billed to residential and commercial customers from the
latest meter reading date to the end of the accounting period.</font></b></h2>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h2>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">REGULATORY ACCOUNTING</font></u></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s accounting policies and practices are
generally the same as used by unregulated companies for financial reporting
under GAAP.&#160; However, Statement of
Financial Accounting Standards (FAS) No.&nbsp;71, &#147;Accounting for the Effects
of Certain Types of Regulation&#148;, requires regulated companies to apply
accounting treatment intended to reflect the financial impact of
regulation.&#160; For example, in establishing
the rates to be charged to the Company&#146;s retail customers, the WUTC and the
OPUC may not allow the Company to charge its customers for recovery of certain
expenses in the same period they are incurred.&#160;
Instead, rates are expected to be established to recover costs that were
incurred in a prior period.&#160; In this
situation, following FAS No.&nbsp;71 requires the Company to defer these costs
and include them as regulatory assets on the balance sheet.&#160; In the subsequent period when these costs are
recovered from customers, the Company then amortizes these costs as expense in
the income statement in an amount equivalent to the amounts recovered.&#160; Similarly, certain revenue items, or cost
reductions, may be deferred as regulatory liabilities, which are later
amortized to the income statement as customer rates are reduced.&#160; In order to apply the provisions of FAS No.&nbsp;71,
the following conditions must apply:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>An independent regulator approves the company&#146;s
customer rates.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The rates are designed to recover the company&#146;s
costs of providing the regulated services or products.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>There is sufficient demand for the regulated
service to reasonably assure that rates can be set at a level to recover the
costs.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company periodically assesses whether
conditions merit the continued applicability of FAS No.&nbsp;71.&#160; In the event the Company should determine in
the future that all or a portion of its regulatory assets and</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">20</font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">liabilities no longer meet the above criteria, it
would be required to write off the related balances of its regulatory assets
and liabilities and reflect the write-off in its income statement.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">PENSION PLANS</font></u></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has a defined benefit
pension plan substantially covering all union employees and salaried employees
hired before September&nbsp;30, 2003.&#160;
The Company also provides executive officers with supplemental
retirement, death and disability benefits.&#160;
These plans were amended in fiscal 2003 so that, subsequent to September&nbsp;30,
2003, benefits under these plans no longer accrue to non-bargaining-unit
employees and officers.&#160; The pension plan
remains substantially unchanged for bargaining-unit employees at this time.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s pension
costs for these plans are affected by the amount of cash contributions to the
plans, the return on plan assets, and by employee demographics including age,
compensation, and length of service.&#160;
Actuarial formulas are used in the determination of pension costs and
are affected by actual plan experience and assumptions of future
experience.&#160; Key actuarial assumptions
include the expected return on plan assets, the discount rate used in
determining the projected benefit obligation and pension costs, and the assumed
rate of increase in employee compensation.&#160;
Changes in these assumptions may significantly affect pension
costs.&#160; Changes to the provisions of the
plans may also impact current and future pension costs.&#160; Changes in pension plan obligations resulting
from these factors may not be immediately recognized as pension costs, but
generally are recognized in future years over the remaining average service
period of pension plan participants.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s funding
policy is to contribute amounts equal to or greater than the minimum amounts
required to be funded under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act, and
not more than the maximum amounts currently deductible for income tax purposes.&#160; The Company contributed $3,365,000 in 2005
and $3,843,000 in 2004 to the pension and supplemental executive retirement
plans, and expects to contribute approximately $3,320,000 in 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The discount rate the
Company selects is based on the average of the 20-year and above Aa debt yields
published by Moody&#146;s.&#160; These are yields
considered to be consistent with the expected term of pension benefits.&#160; At September&nbsp;30, 2005, the Company used
a discount rate of 5.50%, down from the 6.00% rate used at September&nbsp;30,
2004.&#160; A reduction in the discount rate
results in increases in projected benefit obligation, pension liability, and
pension costs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In selecting an assumed
long-term rate of return on plan assets, the Company considers past performance
and economic forecasts for the types of investments held by the plan.&#160; In 2005 and 2004, the Company&#146;s assumed rate
of return on plan assets was 8.25%.&#160; A
reduction in the assumed rate of return would result in increases in pension
liability and pension costs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">DERIVATIVES</font></u></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company accounts for
derivative transactions according to the provisions of Statement of Financial
Accounting Standards (FAS) No.&nbsp;133, &#147;Accounting for Derivative Instruments
and Hedging Activities&#148;, as amended.&#160;
These standards require that the fair value of all derivative financial
instruments be recognized as either assets or liabilities on the Company&#146;s
balance sheet and the recognition of unrealized gains and losses in Other
Comprehensive Income or in the calculation of Net Income, depending on the
nature of the hedge.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Most
of the Company&#146;s contracts for purchase and sale of natural gas qualify for the
normal purchase and normal sales exception under FAS No.&nbsp;133, and are not
required to be recorded as derivative assets and liabilities.&#160; Accordingly, the Company recognizes revenues
and expenses on an accrual basis, based on physical delivery of natural
gas.&#160; The Company applies mark-to-market
accounting to financial derivative contracts.&#160;
Periodic changes in fair market value of derivatives associated with supplies
for non-core customers are recognized in earnings or, if hedge accounting is
applied, in Other Comprehensive Income.&#160;
The Company applies FAS No.&nbsp;71 to periodic changes in fair market
value of derivatives associated with supplies for core customers and records an
offset in regulatory asset and regulatory liability accounts.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">New
Accounting Standards</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Information on new
accounting standards is included in the Notes to the Consolidated Financial
Statements contained in Part&nbsp;II, Item 8, of this report.</font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><a name="Item7a_QuantitativeAndQualitative_170217"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item
7A.&#160; Quantitative and Qualitative
Disclosures About Market Risk</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has evaluated
its risk related to financial instruments whose values are subject to market
sensitivity.&#160; The Company has fixed-rate
debt obligations but does not currently have derivative financial instruments
subject to interest rate risk.&#160; Cascade
makes interest and principal payments on these obligations in the normal course
of its business and may redeem these obligations prior to normal maturities if
warranted by market conditions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s natural gas
purchase commodity prices are subject to fluctuations resulting from weather,
congestion on interstate pipelines, and other unpredictable factors.&#160; The Company&#146;s Purchased Gas Cost Adjustment
(PGA) mechanisms assure the recovery in customer rates of prudently incurred
wholesale cost of natural gas purchased for the core market.&#160; The Company primarily utilizes financial
derivatives, and to a lesser extent, fixed price physical supply contracts to
manage risk associated with wholesale costs of natural gas purchased for
customers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">With respect to
derivative arrangements covering natural gas supplies for core customers,
periodic changes in fair market value are recorded in regulatory asset or
regulatory liability accounts, pursuant to authority granted by the WUTC and
OPUC, recognizing that settlements of these arrangements will be recovered
through the PGA mechanism.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For derivative
arrangements related to supplies for non-core customers, which are not covered
by a PGA mechanism, periodic changes in fair market value are recognized in
earnings or in Other Comprehensive Income.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><a name="Item8_FinancialStatementsAndSuppl_170221"></a><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 8.&#160;&#160;
Financial Statements and Supplementary Data</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 8.65pt;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-8.65pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">REPORT
OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">To the Board of Directors
and Stockholders of<br>
Cascade Natural Gas Corporation<br>
Seattle, Washington</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have audited the
accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Cascade Natural Gas Corporation and
subsidiaries (the&nbsp;&#148;Company&#148;) as of September&nbsp;30, 2005 and 2004, and
the related consolidated statements of income and comprehensive income, common
shareholders&#146; equity, and cash flows for each of the three years in the period
ended September&nbsp;30, 2005. Our audits also included the consolidated
financial statement schedule&nbsp;listed in the Index as Item&nbsp;15. These
consolidated financial statements and the consolidated financial statement schedule&nbsp;are
the responsibility of the Company&#146;s management. Our responsibility is to
express an opinion on the consolidated financial statements and the
consolidated financial statement schedule&nbsp;based on our audits.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We conducted our audits
in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight
Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the
audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are
free of material misstatement. An audit includes examining, on a test basis,
evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. An
audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant
estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall financial
statement presentation. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis
for our opinion.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In our opinion, such
consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the
financial position of Cascade Natural Gas Corporation and subsidiaries as of September&nbsp;30,
2005 and 2004, and the results of their operations and their cash flows for
each of the three years in the period ended September&nbsp;30, 2005, in
conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States
of America. Also, in our opinion, such consolidated financial statement
schedule, when considered in relation to the basic consolidated financial
statements taken as a whole, presents fairly, in all material respects, the
information set forth therein.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></b></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Note 1 - Nature of Business</font></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cascade Natural Gas
Corporation (the Company) is a local distribution company (LDC) engaged in the
distribution of natural gas.&#160; The Company&#146;s
service territory consists of towns in Washington and Oregon, ranging from the
Canadian border in northwestern Washington to the Idaho border in eastern
Oregon.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of September&nbsp;30,
2005, the Company had approximately 196,000 residential customers, 30,000
commercial customers, and 719 industrial and other larger customers.&#160; Approximately 200 of the larger industrial
customers are non-core customers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Residential, commercial,
and smaller industrial customers are core customers who take traditional &#147;bundled&#148;
natural gas service, which includes supply, peaking service, and upstream
interstate pipeline transportation.&#160;
Sales to core customers account for approximately 24% of gas deliveries
and 71% of operating margin.&#160; The Company&#146;s
sales to its core residential and commercial customers are influenced by
fluctuations in temperature, particularly during the winter season.&#160; A warm winter season will tend to reduce gas
consumption.&#160; Over the longer term, these
fluctuations tend to offset each other, as rates charged to customers are
developed based on the assumption of normal weather.&#160; However, consumption is also influenced by
energy efficiency of customers&#146; appliances as well as consumer decisions to
reduce natural gas usage in response to higher prices.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Non-core customers are
generally large industrial, electric generation, and institutional customers
who have chosen &#147;unbundled&#148; service, meaning that they select from among
several supply and upstream pipeline transportation options, independent of the
Company&#146;s distribution service.&#160; The
Company&#146;s margin from non-core customers is derived primarily from this
distribution service, as well as gas management services.&#160; The principal industrial activities of its
customers include the generation of electricity, processing of food, processing
of forest products, production of chemicals, and refining of crude oil.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is subject to
regulation of most aspects of its operations by the Washington Utilities and
Transportation Commission (WUTC) and the Oregon Public Utility Commission
(OPUC).&#160; It is subject to regulatory risk
primarily with respect to recovery of costs incurred.&#160; Various deferred charges and deferred credits
reflect assumptions regarding recovery of certain costs through temporary
customer rate adjustments during future periods.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h3 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Note 2 - Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font></b></h3>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company&#146;s accounting records and practices conform to the requirements of the
uniform system of accounts prescribed by the WUTC and the OPUC.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Principles
of consolidation:</font></b>&#160; The
consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Cascade Natural Gas
Corporation and its wholly-owned subsidiaries:&#160;
Cascade Land Leasing Co.; CGC Properties,&nbsp;Inc.; CGC Energy,&nbsp;Inc.;
and CGC Resources,&nbsp;Inc.&#160; All
inter-company transactions are eliminated in consolidation.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Utility
plant:</font></b>&#160; Utility plant
is stated at the historical cost of construction or purchase.&#160; These costs include payroll-related costs
such as taxes and other employee benefits, supervisory costs, general and
administrative costs, and the cost of funds used during construction.&#160; Maintenance and repairs of property, and
replacements and renewals of items deemed to be less than units of property,
are charged to operations.&#160; Units of
utility plant, retired or replaced, are credited to property accounts at
cost.&#160; Such amounts plus removal cost,
less salvage, are charged to accumulated depreciation.&#160; In the case of a sale of non-depreciable
property or major operating units, the resulting gain or loss on the sale is
included in earnings.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Depreciation
of utility plant is computed using the straight-line method.&#160; The Company periodically conducts
depreciation studies to establish and update asset depreciation lives.&#160; Asset lives used for computing depreciation
range from six to seventy years, and the weighted average annual depreciation
rate is approximately 3.0%.&#160; The Company
periodically reviews the carrying amount of its utility plant and other
long-lived assets for impairment.&#160; An
asset is considered impaired when estimated future cash flows are less than the
carrying amount of the asset.&#160; In the
event the carrying amount of such asset is deemed not recoverable, the asset is
adjusted to its fair value.&#160; Fair value
is determined based on discounted future cash flow.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company periodically
reviews items, such as its franchises and easements, which may give rise to
asset retirement obligations (ARO).</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">30</font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">

<hr size="2" width="100%" noshade color="gray" align="left">

</font></div>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Investments
in non-utility property:</font></b>&#160;
Real estate, carried at the lower of cost or estimated net realizable
value, is the primary investment.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Cash and
cash equivalents:</font></b>&#160; For
purposes of reporting cash flows, the Company accounts for all liquid
investments with a purchased maturity of three months or less as cash
equivalents.&#160; The following provides
additional information to the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows:</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Materials,
supplies and inventories:</font></b>&#160;
Materials and supplies for construction, operations, and maintenance are
recorded at cost.&#160; Inventories of natural
gas are recorded at lower of cost or market.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Regulatory
accounts:</font></b>&#160; The Company
follows Statement of Financial Accounting Standards (FAS) No.&nbsp;71, &#147;Accounting
for the Effects of Certain Types of Regulation&#148;.&#160; This statement provides for the deferral of
certain costs and benefits that would otherwise be recognized in revenue or
expense, if it is probable that future rates will result in recovery from
customers or refund to customers of such amounts.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under Non-current Assets,
regulatory assets related to Unamortized loss on reacquired debt, Gas supply
hedging, and Other are included on the Consolidated Balance Sheets in &#147;Other
Deferred Charges&#148;.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Revenue
recognition:</font></b>&#160; The
Company recognizes operating revenues based on deliveries of gas to
customers.&#160; This includes estimated
revenues for gas delivered but not billed to residential and commercial
customers from the latest meter-reading date to the end of the accounting period.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Allowance
for doubtful accounts:</font></b>&#160;
With respect to its residential and commercial customer accounts, the
Company establishes an allowance for doubtful accounts based on historical
trends and ratios of write-offs to revenues.&#160;
With respect to industrial customer accounts, which are generally
significantly larger than</p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">residential and
commercial, a specific allowance is established for accounts determined to be
at risk of collection.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Leases:</font></b>&#160; The Company leases a portion of its vehicle
fleet.&#160; These leases are classified as
operating leases.&#160; The Company&#146;s primary obligation
under these leases is for a twelve-month period, with options to extend the
lease thereafter.&#160; Commitments beyond one
year are not material.&#160; Rent expense
under operating leases totaled $641,000, $776,000, and $835,000 for fiscal
years ended September&nbsp;30, 2005, 2004, and 2003, respectively.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Federal
income taxes:</font></b>&#160; Deferred
income taxes are determined using the asset and liability method, under which
deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured based upon the temporary
differences between the financial statement and income tax bases of assets and
liabilities, using currently enacted tax rates.&#160;
The Company normalizes temporary differences between book income and
taxable income, with the exception of depreciation differences on assets placed
in service prior to 1981, consistent with the policies of the WUTC and
OPUC.&#160; With respect to utility plant
placed in service after 1980, the Company calculates its deferred income tax
provision to conform to the Federal normalization requirements, as approved by
the WUTC and OPUC.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Investment
tax credits:</font></b>&#160;
Investment tax credits were deferred and are amortized over the
remaining life of the properties that gave rise to the credits.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Use of
estimates:</font></b>&#160; The
preparation of financial statements, in conformity with accounting principles
generally accepted in the United States of America, requires management to make
estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and
liabilities, and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities, at the date
of the financial statements, and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses
during the reporting period.&#160; Actual
results could differ from these estimates.&#160;
The Company has used estimates in measuring certain deferred charges and
deferred credits related to items subject to approval of the WUTC and the
OPUC.&#160; Estimates are also used in the
development of discount rates and trend rates related to the measurement of
retirement benefit obligations and accrual amounts, allowances for doubtful
accounts, values of derivative instruments, unbilled revenue, and in the
determination of depreciable lives of utility plant.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Stock-based
compensation:</font></b>&#160; Compensation
cost for stock options is measured as the excess of the market price of the
Company&#146;s stock at the date of the grant over the price the employee must pay
to acquire the stock.&#160; The Company has
accounted for its stock-based compensation using the intrinsic value method
prescribed in Accounting Principles Board Opinion No.&nbsp;25, &#147;Accounting for
Stock Issued to Employees&#148; rather than using the fair-value-based method
prescribed under FAS No.&nbsp;123, &#147;Accounting for Stock-Based Compensation.&#148;&#160; The Company has adopted the disclosure
requirements of FAS No.&nbsp;123.&#160; See
Note 7 for more information about the Company&#146;s stock-based compensation
plan.&#160; Had compensation expense been
determined in accordance with FAS No.&nbsp;123, the Company&#146;s net income and
earnings per share would have been as follows:</p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">net of income tax.&#160; The charges are related to minimum pension
liability adjustments.&#160; See Note 11 for
more information.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Segment
reporting:</font></b>&#160; Management
views the Company as operating as a single segment, that of a local
distribution company in the Pacific Northwest.&#160;
Therefore, the financial statements do not include disclosure of segment
information.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Derivatives:&#160; </font></b>The Company records
derivative transactions according to the provisions of FAS No.&nbsp;133, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">&#147;Accounting for Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities&#148;</font></i>,
as amended by FAS No.&nbsp;138, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">&#147;Accounting for Certain
Derivative Instruments and Certain Hedging Activities&#148;, </font></i>and by<i><font style="font-style:italic;"> </font></i>FAS No.&nbsp;149, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">&#147;Amendment of Statement 133 on Derivative Instruments and Hedging
Activities&#148;</font></i><i><font style="font-style:italic;">.&#160; </font></i>These standards require that the
fair value of all derivative financial instruments be recognized as either
assets or liabilities on the Company&#146;s balance sheet.&#160; Changes during a period in the fair value of
a derivative instrument are required to be included in earnings or other
comprehensive income for the period.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s contracts
for purchase and sale of natural gas generally qualify for the normal purchase
and normal sales exceptions under FAS No.&nbsp;133.&#160; Accordingly, the Company recognizes revenues
and expenses on an accrual basis, based on physical delivery of natural gas.
The Company applies mark-to-market accounting to financial derivative
arrangements.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">With respect to
derivative arrangements covering gas supplies for core customers, periodic
changes in fair market value are recorded in regulatory asset or regulatory
liability accounts, pursuant to authority granted by the WUTC and OPUC,
recognizing that settlements of these arrangements will be recovered through
the Purchased Gas Cost Adjustment (PGA) mechanism.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For derivative
arrangements related to supplies for non-core customers, which are not covered
by a PGA mechanism, the Company elects whether to apply hedge accounting to the
derivative.&#160; If hedge accounting is
applied, periodic changes in the fair market value are recorded in Other
Comprehensive Income (OCI).&#160; Under hedge
accounting, amounts recorded in OCI are reclassified into earnings in the
period the hedged transaction affects earnings.&#160;
If hedge accounting is not applied, periodic changes in fair market
value are recognized in earnings.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NEW
ACCOUNTING STANDARDS</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">FAS
No.&nbsp;151:</font></b>&#160; In November&nbsp;2004,
the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued FAS No.&nbsp;151, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">&#147;Inventory Costs&#148;</font></i>.&#160; This standard is an amendment of Accounting
Research Bulletin (ARB) No.&nbsp;43, clarifying the requirement that abnormal
amounts of idle facility expense, freight, handling costs, and spoilage be
recognized as current period costs.&#160; The
Company does not expect the adoption of this standard on October&nbsp;1, 2005
to have a significant impact on the Company&#146;s financial statements.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">FAS No.&nbsp;123
(revised 2004):&#160; </font></b>In December&nbsp;2004,
FASB issued FAS No.&nbsp;123 (revised 2004), <i><font style="font-style:italic;">&#147;Share-Based
Payment</font></i>&#148;.&#160; This statement is a
revision of FAS No.&nbsp;123, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">&#147;Accounting
for Stock-Based Compensation&#148;</font></i>, and supersedes Accounting Principles
Board (APB) Opinion No.&nbsp;25, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">&#147;Accounting
for Stock Issued to Employees&#148;</font></i>.&#160;
The Company will adopt this standard effective October&nbsp;1,
2005.&#160; Under FAS No.&nbsp;123 (revised 2004),
the Company will be required to recognize as expense the fair value of equity
instruments, including stock options, to be issued in exchange for goods or
services.&#160; Adoption of this standard is
not expected to have a significant impact on the Company&#146;s financial
statements.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">FAS
No.&nbsp;153:</font></b>&#160; In December&nbsp;2004,
FASB issued FAS No 153, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">&#147;Exchanges of
Nonmonetary Assets&#148;.&#160; </font></i>This
standard is an amendment of APB Opinion No.&nbsp;29 and eliminates certain
exceptions to the requirement of measuring exchanges of nonmonetary assets
based on the fair value of assets exchanged.&#160;
Adoption of this standard on July&nbsp;1, 2005 did not have an impact on
the Company&#146;s financial statements.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">FIN
47:&#160; </font></b>In March&nbsp;2005,
the FASB issued FASB Interpretation (FIN) No.&nbsp;47, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">&#147;Accounting for Conditional Asset Retirement
Obligations&#148;</font></i>.&#160; This standard
is an interpretation of FAS No.&nbsp;143 and was issued to clarify requirements
under FAS 143 regarding the recognition and measurement of asset retirement
obligations.&#160; The Company is evaluating
the impact of FIN 47 and is required to apply the standard no later than September&nbsp;30,
2006.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">FAS
No.&nbsp;154:</font></b>&#160; In May&nbsp;2005,
FASB issued FAS No 154, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">&#147;Accounting for
Changes and Error Corrections&#148;.</font></i>&#160;
This standard replaces APB Opinion No.&nbsp;20 and FAS No.&nbsp;3.&#160; The Company will be required to adopt this
standard October&nbsp;1, 2006.&#160; The
Company is evaluating the impact of this standard.</p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">33</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h1 align="left" style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:left;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Note
3 &#150; Restatement of Prior Years</font></b></h1>

<h1 align="left" style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:left;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h1>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Subsequent to the
issuance of its financial statements for the year ended September&nbsp;30,
2004, the Company determined that its deferred income tax liability was
understated by $930,000 as a result of errors in the calculation of deferred
income taxes associated with the Company's pension plan assets and liabilities,
which caused an understatement of the provision for deferred taxes for each of
the years ended September&nbsp;30, 2001, 2002, and 2003, of $242,000, $304,000,
and $384,000, respectively.&#160; As a result,
the accompanying 2004 and 2003 consolidated financial statements have been
restated from the amounts previously reported.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

Company's Consolidated Financial Statements:</font></p>

<h1 align="left" style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:left;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Note
7 &#150; Stock-Based Compensation</font></b></h1>

<h1 align="left" style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:left;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h1>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the Company&#146;s stock
incentive plan, officers and other key management employees may be granted
options to purchase stock or other equity-based incentives.&#160; The grants vest 1/3 per year over three
years.&#160; Options granted in 2001 expire
five years after the grant date.&#160; Options
granted in 2002 expire ten years from the grant date.&#160; No options were granted in 2003, 2004, or
2005.&#160; The weighted average remaining
life of options outstanding at September&nbsp;30, 2005 is 4.1 years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The 5.21% Notes due September&nbsp;2020
are redeemable at the option of the Company, in whole or in part, at a redemption
price determined under &#147;make-whole&#148; provisions described in the prospectus
supplement.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The 7.50% Notes due November&nbsp;2031
are subject to redemption at the option of the representative of a deceased
beneficial owner.&#160; The maximum required
redemption per deceased beneficial owner is $25,000, principal amount, and
$1,200,000 for all deceased beneficial owners of the Notes.&#160; The 7.50% Notes due November&nbsp;2031 are
redeemable at the option of the Company, in whole or in part, on or after November&nbsp;15,
2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The 5.25% Insured
Quarterly Notes due February&nbsp;2035 are redeemable at the option of the
Company, in whole or in part, on or after February&nbsp;1, 2010.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Annual obligations for
redemption of long-term debt and current maturities are as follows:&#160; none in fiscal year 2006, $8,000,000 in
fiscal year 2007, none in fiscal years 2008, 2009, and 2010, and $165,840,000
thereafter.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There are $89 million
Medium-Term Notes (MTN&#146;s) outstanding as of September&nbsp;30, 2005.&#160; The 5.21% Notes due September&nbsp;2020, the
7.50% Notes due November&nbsp;2031, and the 5.25% Insured Quarterly Notes due February&nbsp;2035
were issued under a 2001 shelf registration providing ability to issue up to
$150 million long-term debt and equity securities.&#160; As of September&nbsp;30, 2005, that
registration statement has $65 million available for issuance.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A deferred income tax
charge (benefit) associated with accruals of minimum pension liability is
included in Other Comprehensive Income (OCI) for each year ended September&nbsp;30
as follows:&#160; $56,000 in 2005, $448,000 in
2004, and ($937,000) in 2003.&#160; See Note
11 for more information on OCI.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred income taxes
reflect the net tax effects of temporary differences between the carrying
amounts of assets and liabilities for financial reporting purposes and the
amounts used for income tax purposes.&#160;
There is no deferred tax provision for temporary differences related to
depreciation of pre-1981 assets because, with respect to those assets, there is
no regulatory recognition of deferred tax accounting.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred tax assets and liabilities are calculated under FAS No.&nbsp;109,
&#147;Accounting for Income Taxes&#148;.&#160; FAS No.&nbsp;109
requires recording deferred tax balances, at the currently-enacted tax rate,
for all temporary differences between the book and tax bases of assets and
liabilities, including temporary differences for which no deferred taxes had
been previously provided because of use of flow-through tax accounting for
rate-making purposes.&#160; Because of prior
and expected future rate-making treatment of temporary differences for which
flow-through accounting has been utilized, a regulatory liability for income taxes
payable through future rates related to those temporary differences has been
established.&#160; At September&nbsp;30, 2005,
the balance of this regulatory liability is $7,044,000.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Note 11 - Retirement
Plans</font></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has a noncontributory defined benefit pension
plan that covers substantially all employees over 21 years of age with one year
of service.&#160; Under a plan amendment
effective October&nbsp;1, 2003, non-bargaining-unit employees no longer accrue
benefits under the plan.&#160; Benefits
accrued as of that point were frozen for those employees.&#160; Employees covered by a bargaining agreement
accrue benefits based on a formula that includes credited years of service and
the employee&#146;s annual compensation.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has also
provided executive officers with supplemental retirement, death, and disability
benefits.&#160; This plan was also frozen September&nbsp;30,
2003 for further accruals and for new participants.&#160; Under the plan, vesting occurred on a stepped
basis with full vesting at age 55 and completing either five years of
participation under the plan or seventeen years of employment with the Company,
upon death, or upon a change in control.&#160;
The plan supplemented the benefit received through Social Security and
the defined benefit pension plan so that the total retirement benefits would be
equal to 70% of the executive&#146;s highest salary during any of the five years
preceding retirement.&#160; The plan also
provides a death benefit equivalent to ten years of vested benefits.&#160;&#160; The employment contracts for the recently
hired Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer provide for a supplemental
defined-contribution retirement plan which is being established that provides
for a retirement income target of 55% of final pay after taking into
consideration benefits earned from other retirement plans and Social Security.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has an Employee
Savings Plan and Retirement Trust (401(k) plan).&#160; All employees 21 years of age or older with
one full year of service are eligible to enroll in the plan.&#160; Under the terms of the plan, the Company
matches contributions based on a percentage of each employee&#146;s contribution up
to 6% of the employee&#146;s compensation, as defined.&#160; Effective July&nbsp;1, 2003, the Company&#146;s
matching contribution percentage was reduced from 75% to 50% with respect to
non-bargaining-unit employees.&#160; The rate
remains at 75% for bargaining-unit employees for the duration of the current
contract with the union.&#160; The Company
recognized costs for matching contributions of $621,000, $728,000, and
$782,000, for 2005, 2004, and 2003, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition to the
existing match of non-bargaining-unit employee contributions, the Company
contributes 4% of eligible salaries, and a 1% to 4% transition contribution, to
employee retirement accounts.&#160; The
Company recognized $956,000 and $973,000 for 2005 and 2004, respectively, under
this plan.&#160; Additionally, there will be
annually determined &#147;profit-sharing&#148; contributions based on the Company</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">39</font></p>

targets.&#160; There was no profit-sharing
contribution for 2005 or 2004.&#160; The retirement
plans remain unchanged for bargaining-unit employees until the existing

<h3 align="center" style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Employee Pension Plan</font></b></h3>

<h3 align="center" style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></h3>

<h1 align="left" style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:left;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Investment
Policy Summary</font></b></h1>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The fundamental
investment objective of the Employee Pension Plan (the Plan) is to provide a
rate of return sufficient to fund the retirement benefits under the plan at a
reasonable cost to the plan sponsor, Cascade Natural Gas Corporation.&#160; At a minimum, the rate of return should equal
or exceed the discount rate assumed by the plan&#146;s actuaries in projecting the
funding cost of the plan under applicable ERISA standards. To do so, the Company&#146;s
Pension Committee (the Committee) may appoint one or more investment managers
to invest all or portions of the assets of the Plan (collectively referred to
as the &#147;Fund&#148;) in accordance with specific investment guidelines, objectives,
standards, and benchmarks.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Because the Committee
expects the Fund&#146;s investment income, when combined with anticipated
contributions by the Company, to exceed the sum of benefit payments and
expenses over the next several years, the Committee intends that the Fund be
managed to achieve long-term returns, with only a small percentage of the Fund
invested in cash.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Fund is divided into
the following segments based on the guidelines below:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Expected Long-term Rate of Return

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The expected long-term rate of return on assets
assumption is based on historical experience and consultation with the

and expected returns attributable to each category of assets over a 20-year
time horizon.</font></p>

<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Expected Long-term Rate of Return
on Plan Assets</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The expected long-term rate of return on assets
assumption is based on historic experience with the investment manager and
consultation with the Company's actuarial consultants.&#160; Factors considered include asset allocation
and expected returns attributable to each category of assets over a 20-year
time horizon.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Retiree
Medical Plans</font></b></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h6 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Investment Policy Summary</font></b></h6>

<h6 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h6>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The fundamental
investment objective of the Trusts (voluntary employee benefit associations
within the meaning of Section&nbsp;501(c)(9) of the Internal Revenue Code) is
to provide assets sufficient to fund medical benefits under the Company&#146;s
medical plan at a reasonable cost to the plan sponsor, Cascade Natural Gas
Corporation.&#160; The Company has appointed a
qualified actuary to determine the benefit obligation under the medical plan
(including post-retirement benefits) and the necessary funding to meet those
obligations.&#160; In performing this
analysis, the actuary has used appropriate actuarial methods for medical
benefits and complies with existing financial accounting standards.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Expected
Long-term Rate of Return on Plan Assets</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The expected long-term rate of return on assets
assumption is based on historical experience and consultation with the
Company&#146;s actuarial consultants.&#160; Factors
considered include asset allocation and expected returns attributable to each
category of assets over a 20-year time horizon.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 12 -
Commitments and Contingencies</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h1 align="left" style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:left;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Gas
Service Contracts</font></b></h1>

<h1 align="left" style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-align:left;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h1>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has entered
into various long-term contracts for natural gas supply, transportation,
storage, and peaking services.&#160; These
contracts are intended to provide adequate supplies of gas for service to core
customers and to meet obligations under long-term, non-core customer
agreements, and to provide that adequate capacity is available on interstate
pipelines for the delivery of these supplies.&#160;
These contracts have maturities ranging up to 25 years, and generally
provide for monthly and annual fixed demand charges, and minimum purchase
obligations.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<hr size="2" width="100%" noshade color="gray" align="left">
